Remark H.7: bootstrap Remark
nodes.statement:
The bounds in Lemma~H.3 (kernel stability), Lemma~H.5 (FFN drift), and Theorem~I.2 (exponential loss decay) are proved {\it conditional} on each other through the per-step inequalities in Lemma~G.1 (Parts~5,~9--13): kernel stability assumes the parameters stay inside the lazy ball; the lazy-ball drift bound $R=O(1/(\sqrt m\,\omega\lambda N))$ assumes exponential loss decay; and exponential loss decay assumes kernel stability. To break this circularity without resorting to a literal substitution chain, we use the standard stopping-time argument of [dzps19].

    Define the stopping time $\tau := \inf\{t \ge 0 : \|\theta(t)-\theta(0)\|_F > R\}$ with $R$ as above, and let $E_t = \{\tau > t\}$ be the event that the trajectory has not exited the lazy ball by time $t$. On $E_t$ all conclusions of Lemma~H.3 and Lemma~H.5 hold by construction; conditional on these, Theorem~I.2 gives ${\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D}) \le \exp(-\alpha\varepsilon^2 s){\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})$ for all $s\le t$. Integrating the gradient-flow drift on $[0,t]$ with this exponentially decaying loss recovers $\|\theta(t)-\theta(0)\|_F \le R/2$, contradicting $\tau \le t$. Hence $\tau = \infty$ almost surely, the lazy ball is never exited, and the three results hold {\it unconditionally} for all $t\ge 0$. This is the precise sense in which the bootstrapping cycle in Figure~fig:proof_dependency closes.
